correctness.rationale: The exact oloid support identity follows from maximizing linear forms on each generating circle and the max identity. It yields all extremizers globally. Four lower charts have max-norm linear width excess with square rescaling and an O(epsilon^3) measure error. Two upper polar charts have uniform quadratic-plus-quartic expansion; the angular mean of the quartic coefficient is 7/32, yielding epsilon/2+epsilon^2/64. Surface Jacobians are exact and ensure the conditional total-variation square/disk limits. Standalone checker independently tested support generators and integrated events at several deficits; finite numerical diagnostics were not used as proof.

value.rationale: The oloid is a classical geometric standard with known mean width but no found sharp rare-direction profile. The result naturally quantifies the extremely narrow and broad orientation frequencies, separates quadratic versus linear rarity, supplies an exact higher-order coefficient, and records different same-circle versus mixed-circle contact types through rigorous limiting distributions. These are geometrically motivated stochastic caliper invariants rather than ad hoc sample or simple normalization.
